n: This psalm likely remembers the return from Babylonian exile. When God brought the captives home, it felt too good to be real — like a dream.

f.w: turned again the captivity of Zion
f.g: Restored Zion’s fortunes; brought back the exiles.

n: They laughed and sang, and even foreign nations admitted, ‘The Lord has done great things for them.’

f.w: The LORD hath done great things for them

n: Israel echoes the nations: yes, the Lord has done great things for us, and we are glad.

f.w: The LORD hath done great things for us

n: Now a prayer for full restoration: refresh us like the dry streambeds of the Negev (‘the south’), which suddenly fill with rushing water after rain.

f.g: Dry wadis in the Negev desert that flood after winter rains.

n: Those who sow with tears will reap with shouts of joy. Sorrow and faithful effort lead to future harvest.

f.w: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy

n: A farmer weeps as he plants precious seed during hard times, but will return singing with armfuls of harvest. Many see in this the work of missionaries and the joy of gathering souls.
